body:
TRUST-ROOT (touches a rails deny-path, so a distinct-provider cross-model approve is required before merge).

`extractTargets` in `plugins/adlc-opencode/rails-checker.mjs` reads `filePath`, `path`, `file`, `files[]`, `edits[]`, and apply_patch envelope bodies. It does NOT read `target`, `targetPath`, or `target_path`, which third-party tools commonly use and which pi's equivalent extractor (`extractToolPaths`, PATH_KEY includes `target`) does recognize.

Surfaced by `adversarial-review --provider codex` on PR #477 (round 10). The handoff-gate half was fixed there — `handoffTargetsOf` in `plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/handoff-gate.mjs` unions the `target` spellings itself — and the rail-policy half was deliberately deferred to this ticket because `extractTargets` also drives per-ticket rail behaviour.

=== THE DEFECT, AS MEASURED ===

The review described this as "custom writers bypass rails". That is NOT what the code does, and building to that description would produce the wrong fix. Measured against `checkToolCall` with `ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1` and a ticket railing `test/**`:

| tool class                                   | `{path: <rail>}` | `{target: <rail>}` |
|----------------------------------------------|------------------|--------------------|
| unknown / mutating (`custom_writer`, `write`) | DENY (rail hit)  | DENY (fail-closed) |
| ungated (`task`, `skill`, `todowrite`)        | DENY (spoof)     | **ALLOW**          |

Unknown and mutating tools are already safe, but by a different mechanism: `checkToolCall` denies any mutating/unknown tool whose args yield ZERO extractable targets while rails are in force ("carries no extractable target path — failing closed"). A `target`-keyed arg yields zero targets, so it fails closed rather than being rail-matched.

The single real hole is the **ungated-tool anti-spoof branch** (`rails-checker.mjs`, the `ungated.includes(name)` block). Ungated tools are allowed by name because they do not write files; the branch exists to catch a tool whose name is in the ungated list but which nevertheless carries a file-path argument resolving to a frozen rail. That defense enumerates targets via `extractTargets`, so the `target` spelling walks straight through it and the call is allowed.

=== REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR ===

1. The ungated-tool anti-spoof branch MUST recognize `target`, `targetPath`, and `target_path` in addition to everything `extractTargets` already covers, and deny when one resolves to a frozen rail.
2. `extractTargets` itself MUST NOT be widened globally. That is the trap in this ticket and the reason it is written down: widening it also changes the mutating/unknown branch, where a `target`-keyed arg currently produces zero targets and therefore a fail-closed DENY. After a global widening, `{target: 'src/in-scope.mjs'}` becomes extractable, misses the rails, and is ALLOWED — the gate gets strictly LOOSER for exactly the tool class it is least able to vouch for. An implementation that makes `extractTargets` itself read `target` closes the reported hole and opens this one; an acceptance criterion below pins `extractTargets`'s output so that outcome fails the build rather than passing quietly.
3. The ungated branch MUST apply the same file-vs-directory distinction `singleFile` already gives mutating tools. Ancestor detection asks whether acting on a DIRECTORY would destroy a rail; applied to a concrete file it over-blocks under an interior-wildcard rail (`src/index.mjs` reads as an ancestor of `src/**/test/*.mjs`). AMENDED after the P5 review measured this: the branch previously passed every candidate to `railHit` with ancestor detection on, which was already over-blocking for `{path: ...}` before this ticket and which widening the recognized shapes would have extended. Everything else keeps its current semantics: the fail-closed behaviour for zero-target mutating/unknown tools, `adlc_gate`'s derived-target denial, the shell classifier, and the handoff deny-set.
4. `handoffTargetsOf` in `lib/handoff-gate.mjs` keeps its own union. It must not be refactored to depend on this change: the deny-set is always-on artifact protection and must not become coupled to per-ticket rail policy.

=== WHY NOT JUST FAIL CLOSED FOR UNGATED TOOLS TOO ===

Do not "fix" this by denying ungated tools that carry no extractable target. `task`, `skill`, `todowrite`, and `question` legitimately carry no file path on almost every call; failing them closed would block ordinary operation whenever rails are in force. The ungated branch allows on zero targets by design, which is precisely why its extraction has to be BROADER than the fail-closed branch's, not narrower.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An ungated tool (`task`, `skill`, `todowrite`, `question`) carrying `{target: <frozen rail>}` is denied, and the reason names the frozen rail. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- The same holds for `targetPath` and `target_path`. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- The test proves it bites: against the pre-fix extraction the `target` case is ALLOWED, asserted against a fixture rather than by inspection. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- An ungated tool carrying a `target` that is NOT a frozen rail is still allowed, so ordinary `task`/`skill` calls keep working while rails are in force. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- A concrete non-rail FILE is not denied as a rail ancestor under an interior-wildcard rail, while a file the rail matches and a directory holding one both stay denied. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- `extractTargets` returns the SAME arrays it does today for every shape, `target` included — i.e. it still does not read `target`. This is the guard on requirement 2. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- A mutating/unknown tool carrying only `{target: ...}` still fails closed with the no-extractable-target reason, whether or not that target is a rail. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs`
- The existing OpenCode rail and handoff contracts pass unmodified. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/*.test.mjs && git diff --quiet origin/main -- plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- The integrations page describes which argument shapes the in-session rail check can see, so an operator can tell what the CI diff gate is backstopping. verify: `rg -q 'target' apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/opencode.mdx`
- The three CI gates pass on a freshly fetched base. verify: `npm run preflight`
- Trust-root tier: a distinct-provider cross-model approve is recorded before merge. verify: `node packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs tier-check --base origin/main --author-provider anthropic`

allow-suppression: none

=== RAILS NOTE ===

`plugins/adlc-opencode/rails-checker.mjs` and `plugins/adlc-opencode/test/rails-checker.test.mjs` are deliberately NOT railed: both must change. Only the slice-5 handoff contract is frozen, because requirement 4 says the deny-set behaviour must not move.

Out of scope: pi's `extractToolPaths` (already reads `target`); the Claude Code and Codex extractors (payload-wide, already cover it); the deny-set / handoff gate in any harness; changing which tool names are ungated, read-only, or mutating; the CI diff gate, which remains the unbypassable backstop for every spelling an in-session scan cannot see.
title: opencode: the ungated-tool rail spoof defense must see target-keyed arguments
